texts: good. the conditional becomes a fireable rule, 'at night' is kept as the time of the showing, and the attracting is tied to each showing occasion.

good. the same fireable rule as the 'when' version; note only that mist-light is recorded as the substance in general rather than as one lantern's particular light, so you cannot later ask about the light of a single showing.

mixed: the denial is captured as a rule covering every nightmoth and it fires, but the parse forgot to record that a nightmoth is a moth - our omission, and no rewrite would change it. 'Ordinary firelight' had to be fused into a single kind name because a bare mass noun gives 'ordinary' nothing of its own to attach to; that reads correctly if you mean ordinary firelight as a kind of light in your world (the counterpart of mist-light), so the wording is fine as it stands.

good. the rarity is recorded twice over - as a low strength and as the word 'rarely' - and the cold night is carried along as the time of the flying, so it reads as 'a nightmoth flying on a cold night is rare', which is what the sentence says.
